subject: Daily AcreetionOS Update -- October 26, 2026
body:
Daily AcreetionOS Update - October 26, 2026

Good morning from Spokane! The team is wrapping up another productive week of development with several infrastructure improvements now live across our repositories. Darren has been hard at work stabilizing the CI/CD pipelines, including a fix for the release workflow indentation issue that was blocking validation in the immutable variant. The GitLab mirror deployment key has also been restored, ensuring our self-hosted infrastructure stays in sync with upstream changes. These backend improvements might not be flashy, but they keep the entire build system running smoothly for every ISO we ship.

On the XLibre front, we pushed a pair of updates this week that refine the graphics stack integration with our Cinnamon desktop environment. The changes focus on input handling improvements and better compatibility with newer hardware configurations that community members have reported. Natalie has also been iterating on the AcreetionMediaWriter tool, adding more robust verification steps for USB writes across different operating systems. We're committed to making the installation experience as reliable as the OS itself.

Security remains a top priority, and we're tracking the latest upstream patches from both AlmaLinux and Debian that landed Friday. The updates cover critical components including OpenSSH, PHP versions across multiple branches, Apache HTTPD, and several system libraries like expat and buildah. Our build pipeline automatically incorporates these fixes into the next ISO refresh, so fresh installs will always have the latest protections. We recommend all users run their regular system updates to pull in these security patches.

Community growth continues to surprise us in the best way. Our Discord server welcomed several new contributors this week, and the first-time contributor welcome message we added to the server repository is already sparking conversations. The GitLab instance is seeing increased activity with issue triage and feature discussions happening in the open. It's incredible to watch a two-person project blossom into a genuine community effort with volunteers stepping up across documentation, testing, and code review.

If you haven't explored our wiki lately, the intelligence sync from this weekend refreshed all guides with the latest configuration examples and troubleshooting steps. We've expanded the hardware compatibility section with community-submitted reports covering everything from Framework laptops to custom desktop builds. The installation guide now includes a dedicated section for dual-boot scenarios with Windows 11, addressing the most common support question we receive. Every guide is version-tagged so you know exactly which release the instructions apply to.

For users running the immutable variant, the updated release workflow means faster, more reliable image delivery with each tagged version. The `-R` flag addition to the release creation step eliminates the unnecessary checkout, shaving minutes off the publish pipeline. You'll also notice shellcheck enforcement on all top-level scripts now, catching potential issues before they reach your system. These quality gates are part of our commitment to repository sovereignty — we verify so you don't have to.

A quick tip for Cinnamon desktop users: the recent XLibre update improves multi-monitor hotplug detection significantly. If you've experienced issues with displays not reconfiguring automatically after docking or undocking, a simple session restart after updating should resolve it. We've also added a new keyboard shortcut reference card to the wiki that covers the custom key
